lessons.title: Choosing Pronouns and Verb Forms
lessons.learn: Hindi marks respect in two places at once: the pronoun (तू, तुम, आप) and the verb that agrees with it. Choosing the right pronoun but leaving the verb in the familiar form is the most common register error at this level. Read every sentence twice: once for the pronoun, once for the verb ending.

vocab.en: respect particle added to a name or word

grammar.title: Pronoun and verb agreement
grammar.explain: आप takes plural verb forms even when one person is addressed: आप आते हैं, आप बोलिए। तुम takes the second-person familiar forms (आते हो, बोलो). तू takes the singular -ता/-ती ending (आता है). The respect of a name is carried by जी, not by the pronoun alone: गुप्ता जी, माँ जी. A respectful pronoun with a familiar verb sounds rude, and a familiar pronoun with a formal verb sounds confused.
grammar.pattern: आप + plural-agreeing verb (हैं, -िए, -ेंगे) · तुम + -ो / -ते form · तू + -ता / -ती form

lessons.title: Requests, Permission and Politeness
lessons.learn: Requests in Hindi are shaped by the verb and by a softening frame. The formal imperative (-िए) and permission questions (क्या मैं … सकता/सकती हूँ?) let you ask without commanding. Politeness at this level means choosing the frame that fits the cost of the request to the listener.

grammar.title: Softened requests
grammar.explain: Use the -िए imperative with आप (बैठिए, लिखिए). Soften with क्या मैं … सकता/सकती हूँ? for permission and क्या आप … सकते/सकती हैं? for help. The conditional frame यदि आपको कष्ट न हो, तो … lowers the cost of the request. The verb सकना agrees with the speaker's gender: सकता for a man, सकती for a woman.
grammar.pattern: क्या + मैं / आप + verb stem + सकता/सकती/सकते + हूँ/हैं ? · यदि आपको कष्ट न हो, तो + polite imperative

lessons.title: Writing a Formal Letter
lessons.learn: Formal Hindi letters follow a stable frame: the addressee line, the subject line, a respectful salutation, a body written in the impersonal passive, and a formal closing. Mastery here is about frame and tone, not long sentences. Keep one register from the first line to the last.

vocab.en: to (the service of) — opening of a formal letter

grammar.title: Frame, passive and closing
grammar.explain: The body uses the impersonal passive to keep the tone objective: निवेदन किया जाता है, सूचित किया जाता है। The salutation depends on the addressee: महोदय for a man in office, महोदया for a woman, and आदरणीय with a name for a known person. Close with सादर or भवदीय, never with the informal आपका मित्र.
grammar.pattern: सेवा में, [title] · विषय: … · आदरणीय / महोदय · body in passive · सादर, [name]

lessons.title: Clauses with कि, जो and जब
lessons.learn: At this level sentences stop being chains of short statements. Hindi builds complexity with subordinate clauses: कि introduces reported or asserted content, जो introduces a relative clause that describes a noun, and जब introduces a time clause. Formal writing often places the subordinate clause first and the main clause after it, marked by वह, वे or तब.

grammar.title: Subordinate clauses
grammar.explain: Use कि after verbs of saying, thinking and knowing: मुझे लगता है कि … and यह स्पष्ट है कि … . Use जो to describe a noun: वह व्यक्ति जो कल आया था … . The head noun is picked up again in the main clause by वह, वे or यह. Use जब for time: जब बारिश रुकी, तब हम निकले। A long जो clause or जब clause needs its correlative (वह / तब) to close it; without it the sentence hangs.
grammar.pattern: जो + clause (describes the noun), वह/वे + main clause · जब + clause, तब + main clause · … कि + reported or asserted clause

lessons.title: Conditions and Concession
lessons.learn: Conditional and concessive clauses let you state what would follow if something happened, or admit a point while holding your position. Hindi uses यदि or अगर with तो for conditions, and चाहे … फिर भी or भले ही … तो भी for concession. The verb in the if-clause is usually in the subjunctive, which is the most common reason learners sound uncertain.

grammar.title: Conditions and concession
grammar.explain: The यदि / अगर clause takes the subjunctive (आएँ, हो, करें) and the main clause with तो states the consequence. चाहे and भले ही introduce a concession, and फिर भी or तो भी mark the contrast in the main clause. बावजूद with a noun means 'despite': इसके बावजूद. Use the subjunctive in these clauses even when the situation is real, because the grammar expresses the hypothetical frame.
grammar.pattern: यदि / अगर + subjunctive, तो + consequence · चाहे / भले ही + subjunctive, फिर भी / तो भी + main clause

examples.en: If you come, we will wait.

examples.en: Even if it rains, the exam will be held.

examples.t: भले ही प्रस्ताव महँगा हो, तो भी इसका लाभ अधिक है।

examples.en: Although the proposal is expensive, its benefit is greater.

mistakes: Using the indicative after यदि in a hypothetical: 'यदि आप आते हो' should be 'यदि आप आएँ'.
Pairing भले ही with बावजूद in the same clause, which repeats the concession.
Omitting the subjunctive in चाहे or भले ही clauses, which makes them sound like plain 'though' statements.

lessons.title: Cause, Result and Purpose
lessons.learn: This lesson separates three relations that learners often blur: cause (क्योंकि, चूँकि), result (इसलिए, अतः, परिणामस्वरूप) and purpose (ताकि, जिससे). Cause and result are about what has happened, so they take the indicative. Purpose is about an intended aim, so it takes the subjunctive. That difference is why ताकि and इसलिए are not interchangeable.

grammar.title: Cause, result, purpose
grammar.explain: क्योंकि and चूँकि give a reason for something already true, with the indicative: वह देर से आया, क्योंकि ट्रेन लेट थी। इसलिए, अतः and परिणामस्वरूप state the consequence, also indicative. ताकि and जिससे state an intended aim, with the subjunctive: उसने जल्दी काम पूरा किया ताकि शाम को छुट्टी मिले। Confusing purpose with result is the most frequent error at this level.
grammar.pattern: कारण: क्योंकि / चूँकि + indicative · परिणाम: इसलिए / अतः + indicative · उद्देश्य: ताकि / जिससे + subjunctive

examples.en: He arrived late because the train was delayed.

examples.en: The train was late, so the meeting did not start.

examples.en: He finished the work quickly so that he would get leave in the evening.

mistakes: Using ताकि with a past indicative result: 'ताकि वह आया' should be a result (इसलिए), not a purpose.
Using इसलिए to express an intended aim: 'वह पढ़ता है इसलिए पास हो' should be 'ताकि पास हो'.
Repeating क्योंकि after a reason has already been stated, which makes the sentence redundant.

lessons.title: Reported Speech
lessons.learn: Reported speech in Hindi introduces what someone said with कि and changes the person of the speaker to third person. Verbs of reporting (कहना, बताना, पूछना) carry the report. A statement uses कि. A yes/no question uses कि or क्या. A wh-question keeps its question word (कब, कहाँ) and drops the question marker. The honorific आप in direct speech usually becomes वे or वह when the speaker is reported.

grammar.title: Indirect speech
grammar.explain: Introduce a statement with कि: उसने कहा कि वह कल आएगा। Shift the first person to the third: 'मैं आऊँगा' becomes 'वह आएगा'. For a yes/no question use कि or क्या: उसने पूछा कि क्या आप आएँगे। For a wh-question keep the question word and drop the question marker: उसने पूछा कि वे कब आएँगे। The honorific आप becomes वे or वह in the report.
grammar.pattern: [speaker] ने कहा / बताया / पूछा + कि + [clause in third person]

examples.r: sacib ne batāyā ki baiṭhak kal hogī.

mistakes: Keeping the original first person in a report: 'उसने कहा कि मैं आऊँगा' is wrong when he is the one who spoke; the report must say वह.
Dropping कि after कहना, which makes the reported clause ambiguous.
Using क्या with a wh-question (कब, कहाँ), which doubles the question marker.

lessons.title: Narrating the Past
lessons.learn: Past narration in Hindi separates three aspects: the simple past (किया), the imperfective past (कर रहा था for in progress, करता था for habitual), and the perfect or pluperfect (कर चुका था for completed before another past event). A good story uses the simple past for the main events and the other aspects for background, habit and what had already happened.

grammar.title: Aspect in narration
grammar.explain: The simple past (गया) marks a completed event. The imperfective past has two forms: कर रहा था (was doing, in progress) and करता था (used to do, habit). The pluperfect कर चुका था shows an event completed before another past event. In a story, the main event is in the simple past, and the background uses the imperfective or pluperfect. Choosing the wrong aspect changes the meaning: वह खड़ा था is 'he was standing', वह खड़ा हुआ is 'he stood up'.
grammar.pattern: [background: imperfective or pluperfect] + जब / तब / तभी + [event: simple past]

examples.r: vah bas sṭāp par khaṛā thā, tabhī bārish śurū ho gaī.
examples.en: He was standing at the bus stop when the rain began.

examples.en: We used to go to the riverbank every Sunday.

examples.en: When he arrived, the fair had already ended.

Using पहले से without a pluperfect verb; the two usually appear together.
Mixing the habit form (जाता था) with the in-progress form (जा रहा था) in one sentence without a clear time frame.

lessons.title: Opinion and Measured Disagreement
lessons.learn: Advanced discussion needs ways to take a position and still show respect for the other side. Hindi uses opinion frames (मेरे विचार में, मुझे लगता है कि), agreement with a limit (मैं सहमत हूँ, परंतु …), and disagreement that softens the claim (आपकी बात सही है, पर …). The skill is to disagree with the claim and its evidence, not with the person.

grammar.title: Opinion and qualified disagreement
grammar.explain: Frame an opinion as yours: मेरे विचार में, मुझे लगता है कि. Show agreement with a limit: मैं आपसे सहमत हूँ, परंतु इसका एक पहलू और भी है। Disagree with the claim, not the speaker: आपका तर्क दिलचस्प है, पर प्रमाण इसके पक्ष में पर्याप्त नहीं है। Use hedges such as शायद, संभवतः and अधिकांशतः to keep the argument proportionate. Do not use both परंतु and पर in one sentence; it doubles the contrast.
grammar.pattern: [opinion frame] + कि + claim, परंतु / पर + limit

examples.t: मेरे विचार में यह नीति उचित है, परंतु इसका क्रियान्वयन कमज़ोर है।
examples.r: mere vicār mẽ yah nītī ucit hai, parantu iskā kriyānvayan kamzor hai.
examples.en: In my view this policy is appropriate, but its implementation is weak.

examples.t: आपकी बात सही है, पर प्रमाण इतने कम हैं कि निष्कर्ष अभी जल्दबाज़ी होगा।
examples.r: āpkī bāt sahī hai, par pramāṇ itne kam haiṃ ki niṣkarṣ abhī jaldbāzī hogā.
examples.en: What you say is right, but the evidence is so limited that a conclusion now would be hasty.

examples.t: मैं इस दृष्टिकोण से असहमत हूँ, क्योंकि यह एक ही आँकड़े पर टिका है।
examples.r: maĩ is dṛṣṭikoṇ se asahmat hū̃, kyoṅki yah ek hī āṅkṛe par ṭikā hai.
examples.en: I disagree with this perspective, because it rests on a single figure.

mistakes: Stating an opinion as an absolute fact: 'यह नीति उचित है' with no frame reads as dogmatic.
Disagreeing with the person (आप गलत हैं) instead of the claim (यह दावा प्रमाण से परे है).
Using परंतु and पर in the same sentence, which doubles the contrast.

culture.text: Hindi has three broad registers that can carry the same idea. Colloquial speech says 'चलो, चलते हैं'. A courteous register, used with strangers and elders, says 'चलिए, चलें?'. Formal writing says 'आपसे निवेदन है कि कार्यक्रम में पधारें'. Official notices, newspaper editorials and government letters rely on the formal register, so reading one short official notice each week is a practical way to absorb it. Choose the register by the listener, not by how well you know the words.

reading.text: पिछले साल मोहल्ले के पुस्तकालय में एक अजीब-सी उलझन पैदा हुई। कुछ सदस्य मानते थे कि नई किताबें ख़रीदना ज़रूरी है, ताकि बच्चे नई दुनिया देख सकें। दूसरे कहते थे कि पहले मौजूदा किताबों की मरम्मत होनी चाहिए, क्योंकि कई पन्ने फट चुके थे। बैठक में एक बुज़ुर्ग सदस्य ने कहा कि दोनों बातें सही हैं, पर बजट छोटा है, इसलिए पहले वह काम हो जिसका असर सबसे जल्दी दिखे। उनकी सलाह मानी गई। अगले तीन महीनों में पुरानी किताबों की मरम्मत हुई, और जब नई किताबें आईं, तब तक बच्चे पुस्तकालय में अधिक समय बिताने लगे थे।

listening.script: नमस्कार। मैं आपको एक छोटा-सा निर्देश देना चाहती हूँ। यदि आप इस कार्यक्रम में भाग लेना चाहते हैं, तो कृपया शनिवार तक अपना नाम दर्ज कराइए। चाहे आप नए हों या पुराने, सभी का स्वागत है। अगर किसी को समय की कठिनाई हो, तो वे हमें लिखकर बताएँ, ताकि हम कोई और विकल्प तय कर सकें।

task.title: One argument, three registers
task.instructions: Choose one local issue, such as traffic or the water supply. Write a paragraph of four to five sentences in three versions: (1) a casual message to a friend, (2) a courteous note to a neighbour, (3) a formal letter to the municipal office. In the formal version use at least one कि-clause, one conditional (यदि or चाहे) and one reported statement. Then write two differences you noticed between the first and the third version.
